the_two_span_change_proposals_in_the_pri.LF_on_P03-008_cut_at_Ezek.16.52: Not carried. MEASURED: neither Ezek.16.51 nor Ezek.16.52 is a member of any of the eleven inventoried formula classes, so no first-order device stands at either candidate seam and the seam cannot be decided by a text device on either placement - LF says as much in its own unresolved-uncertainty field. LF's bearing-of-shame arc is real and I verified it (the shame imperative at 16:52, the purpose clause at 16:54, the perfect at 16:58, one root with the shame noun in the first two). But a counter-arc of the same grade runs the other way across LF's own proposed seam: 16:51 ends on the tsade-dalet-qof root in 'and you justified your sisters' and 16:52 carries that same root three times. An arc that is continuous in both directions across a seam does not decide it. With the devices silent and the arcs two-sided, what remains is the witness: SAMEKH on 16:50 and on 16:58 are the only two marks between the PE on 16:35 and the SAMEKH on 16:63, so the witness reads 16:51-16:58 as exactly one closed section and the shipped span equals it verse for verse. A10 forbids rereading the sectioning to agree with a row; here nothing needs rereading, because it already coincides. LF's cut would place the onset one verse inside a marked paragraph on the strength of one of two arcs.
the_two_span_change_proposals_in_the_pri.LF_on_P03-011_and_P03-012_cut_at_Ezek.17: Not carried. Every underlying fact LF and OL rely on is MEASURED true: Ezek.17.18 is a member of no inventoried class, so no close device stands there; Ezek.17.21 is a member of i_am_yhwh_spoken with the clause verse-final; the as-I-live oath opening 17:19 already stands verse-initially at Ezek.17.16, inside the preceding span; and the oath/covenant/despise/break wording of 17:18 recurs first-person at 17:19. What none of that compels is the merge, because that same lexical chain ALSO runs back into 17:16 - 'who despised his oath and broke his covenant' - so it spans 17:16 through 17:18 into 17:19 and would equally forbid a cut at 17:15/17:16, which nobody proposes. A chain continuous across three consecutive candidate seams tests none of them. What distinguishes the 17:18/17:19 seam is that it has BOTH a witness mark (SAMEKH on 17:18) and an inventoried onset device on its far face (the messenger formula with 'therefore' at 17:19) - more than the 16:51 onset has, which is mark-only, and more than the 18:9/18:10 seam has, which is formula-only. The seam is evidenced and the division stands. The weakness reaches confidence instead, and that is where I send it.
